name: Modal (partial-bank) physical-modelling voice: exciter into one or two resonators defined by a partial model, with material (decay vs frequency), tone (level tilt), hit (random partial emphasis), inharmonic stretch, parallel or series resonators, and velocity/random modulation for a playable mallet or string
goal: Build a playable modal physical-modelling instrument from an exciter and a resonator made of tuned partials. Pick a partial model (string, beam, membrane, vibraphone, open tube or a manual partial list with 1 to 64 partials) and shape it with four relationships from the transcript: decay/release sets how long partials ring; material sets how fast high partials decay relative to low ones (muted vs glassy); tone sets partial level only (a static tilt, different from material); hit changes which partials are boosted at random, like plucking at a different position; and an inharmonic multiplier stretches or compresses partial spacing away from integer harmonics (metallic vs compressed). Choose the exciter (impulse, long exciter, noise): it mostly sets the attack, and a bass-heavy exciter mostly excites low partials. Run two resonators in parallel (blend) or in series (resonator 1 as an extended exciter, e.g. a short-decay drum head into a tube, with optional cross-feedback). Make it playable: velocity to level, material and exciter level; an envelope for a sharper attack over the ringing tail; subtle random on tone, stronger random on hit per note; key → layer gain to lift quiet high notes. More specific than our Karplus-Strong and comb-resonator skills: a modal partial bank with decay-vs-frequency and inharmonicity controls.

source.title: reFX 𝑹𝒊𝒑𝒑𝒍𝒆𝒓 Walkthrough - New Physical Modeling Synth!
source.transcript_note: Sponsored walkthrough; sponsor, price and opinion parts dropped.

prerequisites: Modal/physical-modelling synth with exciter + resonator sections (several free and paid options exist), or Web Audio: a bank of tuned BiquadFilter bandpass (high Q) or decaying sine partials excited by a short noise/impulse buffer (implementation note)
Modulation sources: velocity, envelopes, per-note random, key tracking
Compressor, chorus and reverb for finishing

inputs.name: partial_model
inputs.description: string | beam | membrane | vibraphone | open tube | manual partial list

outputs.name: mod_map
outputs.description: Velocity, envelope, random and key-tracking assignments

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.

Relationships come from the transcript: material = decay timing per partial, tone = partial level only, hit = random partial emphasis, inharmonic multiplier = partial spacing. No numeric presets are given in the video, so set values by ear.
Series mode with high cross-feedback strength can blow up or kill the sound. Raise it slowly.
Sponsored walkthrough. Price and opinion content dropped; the procedure is generic to modal synths.

steps.action: Mute the resonators and raise the exciter's direct output to audition exciters (impulse, long exciter, noise). Then turn the direct output back down and enable resonator 1.
steps.expect: You hear the exciter alone, then only the resonated sound

steps.action: Pick a partial model and partial count for resonator 1 (start with the string model). Try beam, membrane, vibraphone and open tube to hear how partial patterns change the instrument.
steps.expect: Clearly different instrument families from the same exciter

steps.action: Shape the partials: decay/release for ring time; material down = high partials die faster (muted), up = the opposite; tone = cut highs or lows by level only; hit = random partial emphasis (pluck position); inharmonic multiplier up = stretched, metallic partials, down = compressed partials.
steps.expect: Each control changes timbre in a distinct way; material changes decay over time, tone changes static brightness

steps.action: Optional manual mode: edit partial positions and amplitudes (e.g. 4 partials), make two snapshots and use a ratio control to morph between them.
steps.expect: Custom partial set that can morph

steps.action: Add resonator 2. Parallel: same exciter into both, set level and balance. Series: exciter → R1 → R2; use R1 with a very short decay (drum head) as an extended exciter for a tube in R2. Raise cross-feedback strength carefully.
steps.expect: Parallel gives a blend; series gives a new hybrid body

steps.action: Optionally layer the two basic oscillators and route chosen sources through two filters (series or parallel), e.g. filter only the oscillators. Use the second layer for a second, different sound.
steps.expect: Richer hybrid without muddying the resonators

steps.action: Make it playable: velocity → resonator level, material (louder = more high partials) and exciter level; envelope 1 with a fast attack and low sustain/decay → level for a prominent attack over the tail; subtle random → tone; per-note random → hit; for a vibraphone, slow sine LFO → pitch at a very small depth.
steps.expect: Dynamic, slightly varied notes like a real instrument

steps.action: Finish: low-cut a resonator if it gets muddy, then stereo widener, compressor, chorus and reverb. If high notes are quieter, map key tracking → layer gain.
steps.expect: Even level across the keyboard and a finished space

verification: With the resonators off and direct output up, only the exciter is heard; with direct output down, only the resonated tone is heard.
Turning material down makes high partials die faster than low ones, while tone changes brightness without changing decay length.
Raising the inharmonic multiplier gives an audibly metallic, bell-like tone.
Soft and hard notes differ in brightness and level; repeated notes vary slightly (random hit).
